messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: overlap(): "Error in if (DOF == 0) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed"
parts:
Hi Roy,

  1. You imported your datasets separately without supplying a projection argument, so they all have independent, automated projections. I have added an error message when overlap is called on distributions with different projections. This is why the overlaps are all too high.
  2. Especially, with this data, you need to use ctmm.select instead of ctmm.fit. The error was caused by multiplication of infinite variance with zero sensitivity, which equals NaN, because the model was bad with infinite uncertainty on some parameters that didn't have support.
  3. I fixed the error (even with a bad model), so that it will return appropriate CIs and not crash.

The patches should be up on GitHub by tomorrow: which you will be able to install via devtools::install_github("ctmm-initiative/ctmm"). Please report any further issues.

Best,
Chris

I wondered about the lack of a projection argument at first, but when I create shapefiles from the independent AKDE estimates, they project on my base map where they're supposed to. That's what confused me about the overlap estimates.

Thanks, also, for the other feedback.
Roy

parts:
Hi Roy,

The patch is up on Github now.

Yeah, the distributions should export fine with individualized projections. Its just that within ctmm, I hadn't coded overlap() to check that two distributions were in the same projection.

I recall your issue with QGIS. It looked like rgdal (which is what ctmm uses) was correct, while QGIS was incorrect for that projection. You might try a different projection type. You might also try filing a bug report with QGIS.

Best,
Chris
